fields.name: Buckler
fields.description: A compact shield whose material and exact form suit its bearer.

fields.name: Round shield
fields.description: A practical circular shield with an appearance chosen for the setting.

fields.name: Kite shield
fields.description: A broad shield offering ordinary coverage without a fixed heraldry.

fields.name: Reinforced shield
fields.description: A carefully strengthened shield whose construction remains open to interpretation.

fields.name: Tower shield
fields.description: A tall defensive shield adapted to the bearer’s size and fighting style.

fields.name: Dueling shield
fields.description: A responsive shield balanced for active defense and close exchanges.

fields.name: Mirrored shield
fields.description: A polished shield with an unusual surface whose significance is left to the GM.

fields.name: Monster-hide shield
fields.description: A shield incorporating material from a notable creature without prescribing its powers.

fields.name: Folding shield
fields.description: An ingenious shield designed to change profile while keeping its exact mechanism undefined.

fields.name: Guardian shield
fields.description: An exceptional shield associated with protection, its history and effects left open.

fields.name: Stormward shield
fields.description: A remarkable shield carrying stormlike motifs without a predetermined enchantment.

fields.name: Living-wood shield
fields.description: A shield of uncanny wood whose nature and behavior are determined by the GM.

fields.name: Bastion relic
fields.description: A renowned shield remembered as a symbol of an unbroken defense.

fields.name: Eclipse shield
fields.description: A singular shield bearing eclipse imagery and an intentionally undefined legacy.

fields.name: Oathkeeper shield
fields.description: A legendary shield tied to an oath whose bearer, terms, and consequences remain open.

fields.name: Runed shield
fields.description: A carefully made shield bearing a rune of {{ rules.name }}; its precise function is left to the GM.
